Ui.DefaultCulture: WithCulture(...) is optional. Get(key) captures CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture when the builder is created, for both template lookup and MessageFormat formatting. Resolve() and ResolveAsync() use that captured culture. WithCulture(...) overrides it only for this translation and does not change the ambient culture.
Ui.ChangeCulture: Set CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture before Get(...) to change the default for new translations and other components that use the current UI culture. Also set CultureInfo.CurrentCulture to align standard .NET number and date formatting:
Ui.CultureScope: Existing builders retain their captured culture; create a new builder after a change. The current culture belongs to the execution context and flows through task-based asynchronous operations on modern .NET. Components using explicit cultures or cached text need their own update; already rendered UI needs a rerender.
Ui.CultureDefaults: For application-wide thread defaults, set DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture and DefaultThreadCurrentCulture at startup. They do not override explicitly set thread cultures. In ASP.NET Core, configure culture per request/user instead of changing these defaults for each user.
